My tools don’t move themselves, you know? I’m a fabricator, been doing assembly work since I got out of high school, and if you don't keep your station organized, you lose a finger or you lose your job. My old foreman, guy named Mike, he used to walk the floor with this clipboard and just stare at you until you cleaned up your scraps... 

But anyway, it's not just the tools. My fishing plans don’t get spoiled by accident every single weekend. I was supposed to go down to the lake last Saturday. Caught a beautiful bass there a few years back, fought me for a good ten minutes, best day I've had in a long time. The weather was supposed to be perfect for it, too. But after all these months... I can see plain as day he’s been trying to take over my place and push me out.

Dave was a good guy, though, just had a rough patch. He had this old Chevy C10 he was restoring in his garage. Beautiful truck, cherry red. We used to drive out to these swap meets in the county on the weekends looking for original parts. You wouldn't believe the absolute junk people try to sell you at those things, just boxes of rusted bolts and they want top dollar for it. We walked around for hours in the baking sun one time just looking for a specific door handle...

turns.doctor_question: Besides noticing that your tools have moved and your fishing plans getting spoiled, have you heard any voices or seen anything unusual that other people around you couldn't hear or see?
turns.patient_response:
Voices? No, no, I don't hear voices or see things that aren't there. My hearing and eyesight are perfectly fine. Better than most guys my age, actually. You have to have good ears in the shop, you know? You learn to listen to the machines. I can hear when a bearing is starting to go bad on a press before the digital sensors even pick it up. It makes this real subtle whining sound, kind of like... well, kind of like the transmission on my brother-in-law's old Ford Taurus. 

He drove that thing into the ground. Never changed the fluid once. I told him, I said, you gotta maintain your equipment or it's gonna leave you stranded. Sure enough, we were driving up to the state park for a camping trip back in... must have been '04, '05 maybe? Middle of July, hotter than blazes, and the thing just locked up on the highway. We had to sit on the shoulder for three hours waiting for a tow. The guy who finally showed up was eating a meatball sub right there in the cab, got sauce all over the steering wheel. I couldn't believe it. You gotta have respect for your vehicle, you know? It's like a tool. You take care of it, it takes care of you. People just don't have pride in their things anymore. They buy cheap plastic junk and throw it away when it breaks. 

But anyway... what was the question? Did I hear something? No, no voices or anything crazy like that. Just the regular sounds. I just see what's actually happening right in front of me, that's all.

turns.doctor_question: You mentioned your wife's relative is behind this. Can you tell me his name and describe exactly what you've seen him do or how you know he's been in your house?
turns.patient_response:
His name? Well... you know, her family is just huge. Massive. They're mostly from out near the state line, and there's so many cousins and second cousins I can't keep them all straight. We went to a family reunion out there back in, oh, 2012 maybe? Rented out this whole pavilion by the lake. Beautiful spot, but the mosquitoes were just murder. Big as quarters, I swear. My wife's aunt brought this potato salad that sat out in the sun for like four hours. I told her, I said, you can't leave mayonnaise out in ninety-degree heat, but nobody listens to me. Half the family got sick. I was fine, though, because I stuck to the burgers. You gotta cook the meat all the way through, you know? Some of these guys, they flip it once and call it done. That's how you get E. coli. 

We had a guy at the shop who got E. coli from a food truck down the street. He was out for a week and a half. Boss was furious because we were behind on a big order for John Deere. You know they paint all their stuff that specific green? It's trademarked. You can't just go buy John Deere green off the shelf at the hardware store. They have a whole proprietary mixing process for the paint booths. If you don't clean the nozzles on the sprayers right after using it, it gums up the whole line and you're out there with a wire brush for three hours...

Wait, what were you asking me? Oh, right. Her relative. Look, I don't know his exact name right this second, there's just too many of them to keep track of. And I haven't caught him on camera or anything yet. But I know it's one of them. I just know.

Well, I don't... I don't have a specific name, no. I mean, it could be any of them. Like I said, her family is just massive. You go to one of those reunions and it's just a sea of people. You know, speaking of strong features, we were working on this custom chassis last month for a guy who races dirt tracks. He wanted the whole frame reinforced with chromoly tubing. You can't just weld it like regular mild steel, you gotta pre-heat it and then TIG weld it, otherwise the joints get brittle and they'll snap right off when you hit a bump at eighty miles an hour. I've been TIG welding for... oh, gotta be going on twenty-five years now. My hands are still steady as a rock. You gotta have a steady hand, and you gotta control your breathing. It's almost like being a sniper, you know? You get in the zone, under the hood, and it's just you and the puddle of metal. Sometimes I'll be under there for hours and I won't even realize the guys have all gone to lunch. 

They usually go down to this deli on 4th Street. Good pastrami, but they charge an arm and a leg. I always pack my own lunch. You save a lot of money that way, and you know exactly what you're eating. I got this insulated thermos that keeps my soup hot until 2 PM. Best twenty bucks I ever spent... 

But yeah, no, I don't have one specific name for you. It's just one of them. I know it is.

You know, speaking of 24/7, you ever try working a rotating swing shift? Back in '06, the fabrication plant got this massive government contract for aluminum chassis, and they had us running three shifts, 24 hours a day, 7 days a week. I was stuck on the graveyard shift, 11 PM to 7 AM. It completely destroys your internal clock. You're trying to sleep at noon with the sun blazing, and the neighbor's kid is out there revving a two-stroke lawnmower. I bought these heavy blackout curtains, but they always leave that little gap at the edge where the light shoots in like a laser beam right into your eyeball. And the food... man, you end up eating gas station hot dogs at 3 in the morning because nothing else is open. My cholesterol went through the roof that year. I was eating those roller-grill taquitos every night, and the acid reflux was just brutal. You ever try welding overhead when your stomach is on fire? It's miserable...

But anyway, what I'm saying is, it doesn't matter who sits down with me or what they claim they saw. I’m only here in this office because everybody keeps acting like I’m imagining it. My own wife, my boss, whoever—they all treat me like I'm making it up. But I know my wife’s relative came into this house to get at me. They can swear up and down they watched the place, but my tools don’t move themselves! My fishing plans don’t get spoiled by accident every single weekend! After all these months of this happening, I can see it plain as day. He’s been trying to take over my place and push me out, and no little week-long stakeout is gonna change the facts.
